The command docker build . builds a Docker image from a Dockerfile located in your current working directory.
• docker build: Tells Docker to compile a new container image.
• -t live-code-server: Applies a human-readable tag (name) to the image so you can easily reference it later.
• .: Specifies the build context. The dot tells Docker to look for the Dockerfile and source files in your current working directory.
• docker run: Tells Docker to create and start a new container.
• -p 3000:3000: Maps port 3000 on your host machine (left) to port 3000 inside the container (right). This lets you access the app by going to http://localhost:3000 in your web browser.
• live-code-editor: The name of the Docker image you want to run.
